findings.body:
Any authenticated caller can set `body.accountId` and load a different account. The comment says this is for support staff tools, but there is no role, permission, or service-identity check before the override — only `auth(req)`, which previously scoped the read to `caller.accountId`.

Failure mode: attacker with any valid session sends `{"accountId":"victim-id"}` and receives that account via `Response.json(account)` (IDOR).

Require an explicit staff/internal authorization check before honoring `body.accountId`; otherwise always use `caller.accountId`.

summary:
## Verdict

Critical authorization hole: `getAccount` now trusts a client-supplied `accountId` with no staff/role check, so any authenticated caller can read any account.

## Analysis

Previously the handler always loaded `caller.accountId` from `auth(req)`, which scopes the response to the authenticated principal. This PR still authenticates the caller, then overrides the lookup key with `body.accountId` whenever that field is present.

The comment claims the body field is for support staff tools, but nothing in the handler (or elsewhere in this tree) verifies a support role, permission, or service identity before honoring it. Any session that passes `auth` can POST `{"accountId": "<victim>"}` and receive that account record.

That is a classic IDOR / broken-authorization failure on an account-read endpoint. Ship a staff gate (role claim, internal service token, or allowlisted principal) before using the override; keep the `caller.accountId` fallback only for the self-read path.

No other files changed; `auth` / `db` are imported but not present in-repo, so role APIs could not be confirmed beyond the missing check in this handler.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The patch replaces a caller-scoped lookup (`caller.accountId`) with `body.accountId ?? caller.accountId` and returns that account with no staff/role check after `auth(req)`, so any authenticated client can IDOR another account.
